text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A26, A27 and A28 each ran in all 200 traces, clustered around position 0.37 of the trace; the three always appeared together (in 100 in 100 traces) without a fixed order among themselves, and A26 preceded A29 in about 98 in 100 traces. In the later window they are nearly gone: A26 in 2, A27 in 1 and A28 in 2 of 200 traces. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL031, REL033, REL035, REL036, REL038]
- A19 and A20 were not observed at all in the earlier window, and A21 in only 1 trace; in the later window they occur in about 31, 34 and 37 in 100 traces respectively, around position 0.36 of the trace. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- A44's successors changed almost completely: earlier, about 94 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A26, A27 or A28; later, about 93 in 100 go to A19, A20 or A21. A44 itself still occurs in every trace in both windows, slightly later in the trace (mean position about 0.31 to 0.33). [DIR007, POS008]
- The three new activities behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: any pair of them co-occurs in at most about 2 in 100 later traces, and each leads to A29 in about 97 in 100 of its outgoing transitions. A44 precedes them in about 30–37 in 100 traces, and they precede A29 in about 31–37 in 100 traces. [REL013, REL014, REL020, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL019, REL025, REL030, REL018, REL024, REL029]
- A29 still occurs in every trace in both windows and sits slightly earlier (mean position about 0.43 to 0.40); the distance from A44 to A29 shrinks from about 4 steps (93 in 100 at lag 4) to about 2 steps (92 in 100 at lag 2). [POS007, LAG010]
- A11 and A12 earlier co-occurred with A26/A27/A28 in about 47 in 100 traces (A11 before A26 in about 45); later, A11 occurs in about 56 in 100 traces but together with A26 in only about 1 in 100. [REL004, REL010]
- Several lag items concerning pairs within the old block rest on only 1–2 later observations and carry little weight on their own. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: in the later window, the segment formed by A26, A27 and A28 — previously executed together in every trace between A44 and A29 — is no longer executed, and three mutually exclusive activities, A19, A20 and A21, now occupy that region in roughly a third of cases each, placed after A44 and before A29. The screening produced 64 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.55 expected without any change, far beyond what a stable process yields, and the evidence is direct and consistent: A44's successor profile flips from the old block to the new activities, the positional data show the old block vanishing exactly where the new activities appear, the relational data place A44 before A19/A20/A21 and these before A29, and the A44-to-A29 distance contracts from about 4 to about 2 steps, as expected when an intermediate block disappears. Limitations: many items describe the same underlying trace-level difference rather than independent confirmations; the evidence cannot distinguish outright removal of A26/A27/A28 from them having become optional and skipped in about 99 in 100 later cases, nor rule out that A19/A20/A21 are relabelled versions of the old steps rather than genuinely new ones; and in the roughly two thirds of later traces without A19/A20/A21, the route from A44 to A29 is only indirectly indicated by the shortened lag. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR007, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL013, REL018, REL019, REL024, REL025, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL033, REL035, REL036, REL038, LAG010]

Other differences: A11 and A12, which previously always appeared alongside the old block when they occurred, now run without it. [REL004, REL010]
